source_title: ECI extends SIR timelines in Maharashtra, Delhi, Andhra, Haryana, Telangana, Nagaland
source_excerpt: New Delhi The Election Commission of India (ECI) has re-scheduled the deadline for filing claims and objections in the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in six States including in the national capital Delhi. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/special-intensive-revision-of-electoral-rolls/ While the claims and objections deadline has been extended in Delhi, the window has been reopened in the States of Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Telangana, and Nagaland. Maharashtra SIR: Why are more than 2.07 crore enumeration forms ‘uncollected’? | Explained Maharashtra SIR: Why are more than 2.07 crore enumeration forms ‘uncollected’? | Explained It is to be noted that August 17 is not the final deadline. The first draft of the electoral roll will be published on August 24 and citizens will be allowed to raise claims and objections between August 24 to September 23 Maharashtra SIR: Why are more than 2.07 crore enumeration forms ‘uncollected’? | Explained storyline 1 The decision was conveyed by ECI through separate letters to the state electoral officers of all the States late on Thursday (October 29, 2026). Though the poll panel has extended the date for SIR schedules several times in various States before, Thursday’s (October 29) decision came a day after the Supreme Court which was hearing the Delhi SIR matter suggested it to do so. Claims and objections can now be filed until November 25, instead of October 30 in Delhi. Disposal of claims has been pushed from November 30 to December 15, and the final roll will be published on December 22. Delhi SIR: Over 94% of electors flagged for discrepancies cleared for final electoral roll Delhi SIR: Over 94% of electors flagged for discrepancies cleared for final electoral roll Delhi SIR: Over 94% of electors flagged for discrepancies cleared for final electoral roll storyline 1 The deadline for filing claims and objections, which ended on October 26 in Maharashtra, has been extended to November 13. The notice phase and disposal of claims will now run until November 25, and the final roll will be published on November 30. The notice and resolution period now closes on November 20 for Andhra Pradesh and Haryana; November 25 for Nagaland; and November 26 for Telangana. All four States will publish their final electoral rolls on November 30. All these States underwent the SIR in the Phase 3 which covered a total of 16 States and three UTs. A living voter who is struck off loses their constitutional right The SIR and its error margin storyline 1 Amid widespread protests over the deletion of nearly 13 crore names from pre-SIR voter lists, the ECI has already begun special camps to re-enrol those who have been left out during the SIR. Simultaneously, it has also announced annual Special Summary Revision for those States where the SIR process has been completed, which again means that those who were left out during the SIR can get back into the rolls without the required documentation made mandatory during the SIR.
